To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) RANS simulations can be used to investigate the effects of coal characteristics, burner designs, and combustion conditions on the combustion and emissions, (ii) LES is a useful tool to investigate the effects on coal characteristics, and combustion conditions, and (iii) RANS and LES are complementary tools for the investigation of the pulverized fuel combustion and emissions.

(1) the RANS simulation is useful in predicting the combustion characteristics in the pulverized coal fired boiler, (2) the LES can provide more detailed information of the flow and combustion fields in pulverized coal combustion, and (3) the RANS and LES simulations have a potential to predict and design a combustion system with high efficiency and low emissions.
the CFD of pulverized coal combustion is a powerful tool to understand the complex phenomena and to improve the performance of pulverized coal fired boilers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a CFD code for the prediction of the flow and combustion in the pulverized coal combustors.

the following three subjects: 1) Development of a numerical simulation model of the pulverized fuel combustion for the prediction of the flow and temperature fields, and the formation of pollutants such as NO, SO2, unburned carbon particles and fly-ash particles. 2) Development of the combustion model for the pulverized fuel, and 3) Development of a combustion model for the coal char particles.
the following topics: 1) Numerical simulation of pulverized coal combustion using a RANS approach, 2) Numerical simulation using a LES approach, and 3) Future perspectives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CFD of the combustion is a powerful tool for the development of the pulverized combustion furnace and burners.
CFD of the turbulent pulverized coal combustion is still in its early stage, although it is a very powerful tool to investigate the complex combustion process.

the LES is the most suitable tool for the prediction of the pulverized fuel combustion, although the LES is still in its infancy and the RANS simulation is still a very important tool for the practical design of combustion systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LES simulation is more suitable for the prediction of turbulent combustion than RANS simulation in terms of the prediction of the flame structure, the combustion efficiency and the emission of pollutants.
the LES of pulverized coal combustion has been established to predict the flow field, temperature and concentration of pulverized coal particles and combustion products.
CFD of the coal combustion can be a powerful tool for the development of the pulverized fuel combustion furnaces and for the design of burners for coal fired power plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LES approach can predict the turbulent combustion of pulverized coal in a furnace more realistically than the RANS approach.
the CFD can be used as a useful tool to predict and understand the pulverized coal flames.
CFD simulations of pulverized coal combustion can be a powerful tool to develop and optimize the design of the furnace and burner for the reduction of the environmental pollutant emissions.
